name: Make fresh pasta
blurb: Flour and eggs, nothing else. The whole skill is judging hydration by feel and kneading long enough to develop the gluten, then rolling thin enough.
gear: 00 flour or strong plain flour, and eggs
A rolling pin or a pasta machine
steps: Start with 100 g flour per egg, adjusting by feel — humidity and egg size mean the ratio is a starting point, not a rule.
Make a well, beat the eggs in the centre and gradually pull in flour until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead for a full ten minutes until smooth and elastic. This is longer than feels necessary and is what makes pasta chewy rather than crumbly.
Rest, wrapped, for at least 30 minutes so the gluten relaxes and the dough rolls thin without springing back.
Roll in stages, thinner each pass, dusting lightly — thin enough to see your hand through it.
Cut, dry briefly, and cook in heavily salted water for 90 seconds to three minutes.
tips: Fresh pasta cooks in a fraction of the time of dried. Taste early.
Too much dusting flour makes a gluey sauce later. Use semolina if you have it.
A dough that springs back has not rested long enough. Wait rather than fight it.
proof: Silky, evenly thin pasta with a proper bite, made from scratch without a recipe in front of you.
